reviews.author: ethan ghymn
reviews.text:
I stopped by Gino's New York Pizza once before at the main branch in Itaewon to taste the buffalo wings, and in the restaurant's kitchen, I saw some employees who looked like Koreans, and the taste of the buffalo wings had a somewhat American feel, so I remember eating them as being reasonably good, if not delicious.

Then, yesterday, when I looked at Danyul's review of this store, which was selected as Review of the Day, I found out that Manpple Eat Deal was offering a half-price deal for take-out only. It's hot these days, and it's going to be hot for the family to have dinner at home, so I decided to take it out and try it out, so I scanned pictures of the pizza here and there. It didn't have the crust color and feel of the Italian pizza you expect from New York pizza, but it was a brighter so-called golden brown color with a slightly oily feel. It was a cheaper pizza. It felt like New York pizza? It may be different from the visuals, but it is a popular restaurant and I wanted to try it at least once, so I decided to take advantage of the half-price It Deal opportunity.

When I called to place an order in advance, there was a backlog of orders, so I was told it would take about 25 minutes, so I ordered the Brooklyn Best Large with Manple's monthly half-price deal.

I arrived a little earlier than the pick-up time, and since it was still early in the evening, there were no customers in the store, but the kitchen was quite busy as there were a lot of delivery orders, and the delivery people kept coming in.

I showed the Manple Eat Deal to the clerk and waited while drinking cool water on the other side of the store. I waited a little longer and the Brooklyn Best large size was ready. I brought it home and left it for a while since I didn't have any family members. I opened the box to share it with my family when they came in, but the visual of it felt like it was roughly made rather than like it was made with care by the chef-owner who I like, and the visuals of the toppings didn't look like they were high-quality, so it was momentary.

Perhaps because it was left for a while before eating, it cooled slightly and hardened, but I took one piece off and took a bite, and it was delicious.

I felt it in the pictures I saw here and there, but I thought it couldn't be like that. Rather than the light chewiness of the fresh Italian pizza-like dough that I expected from New York pizza, it felt a little oily and crunchy, so it felt like it was New York pizza. The taste and aroma of the toppings on the pizza were also far from luxurious, so I was skeptical, but it turned out to be just that.

Pecorino Romano cheese is the same, and Italian sausage, which should be very fragrant more than anything, is of low quality or is only added in small portions. It doesn't mean that you can't feel the scent, but it is relatively weak and the taste is also bland, which is disappointing.

If I had eaten it right away at the store, it might have been okay, but I ate it about 30 minutes later and if it tasted like this, it was especially the original price, not the Manple Eat Deal half price deal.
I feel like I would have been angry if I had paid 37,000 won.

That's why a family member who came in after having dinner outside tried only one piece, including the crust, and after tasting it, they said it wasn't good and got up from the table.

I also had dinner, but I only ate two pieces and closed the box lid.

Overall, it seems to be a store that serves American-style pizza for a long time, so I saved it for a while, but I had forgotten about it for a while. I found out about the Manple It Deal package-only half-price deal, so I took advantage of the opportunity to get takeout and taste Brooklyn's Best Pizza. It was an experience that made me realize once again why I like new stores that are full of passion and stay away from stores that are growing in popularity as they become more famous. I don't know if it will become a bad store as expected if it becomes more famous, but from my past experience, it has a much more New York pizza feel. It was a bad experience that made me feel like I should have gone to PizzazWitAttitude right across the street, which was close by.

reviews.author: Lebonah 778
reviews.text: Garosu-gil is one of the fine restaurants that can be said to be the best in Korea in terms of presentation. Thanks to the chef who always pursues an enterprising trend and atmosphere, every meal feels like a truly new world. The recently relocated location is also a very hip place, with easy parking (10,000 won excluding valet fee) and a novelty experience that feels like experiencing a newspaper right from the entrance. As for the architectural characteristics, Mies Banderoe is said to pursue simplicity, but it has a very modern yet classic style, so the atmosphere inside the store is very comfortable and nice. The motif of the two twin circular stairs seems to reflect the owner chef's cooking philosophy of being trendy while not losing its original taste and style. The first floor is a laboratory, cooking class, and workroom. There is also a beautifully created small garden growing natural herbs on one side, and a food space reminiscent of a butcher shop is also nicely located. The second floor is the dining space, and one of the main features of Ryunique is the tableware that has been handcrafted by craftsmen to suit each concept. Many of you will probably come across a new cultural object that you have never heard of at least once or twice (for example, a wet tissue storage box...) However, today's course did not get all the stars because of the feeling that it was not as original as before.

reviews.text:
I had the 200,000 won course la saison for dinner on Sunday.

Service -
I made a reservation for 6 o'clock and my friend arrived 5 minutes later and sat down first. I arrived exactly at 6 o'clock. I thought the waitress would come to take my order, but she didn't, so I was waiting, and about 5 minutes later, a waitress came and asked me bluntly, "Why aren't you taking my order?" I was a little embarrassed because he spoke coldly. Five minutes after ordering a course meal, a male employee came again and asked if I would like to order. Is this a place where employees don't communicate? I wanted to.

I went there pleasantly, but as soon as I sat down, I was served in an unfriendly manner, which made me feel uncomfortable throughout the meal. I had high expectations before making the reservation, and I had received help from an acquaintance, so I went there to treat them, but both I and my acquaintance were dumbfounded, so I was a bit disappointed. Well, I'm not looking for great service, but I think local restaurants are friendlier. There are many French restaurants like this, so I don't think I will come here again next time.

Cooking -
The dish was delicious. But there are so many other, better places to eat, so is it worth it? I'm not sure...

Deposit -
I paid a reservation deposit of 100,000 won, but when I got home and thought about it, what was the refund process? This occurred to me and I was thinking of calling again since I didn't receive any instructions about this from the restaurant.

Atmosphere -
I didn't think the atmosphere was that good either. It's just an ordinary Western restaurant. It's not special. It feels rather old... Can it be described as classic in good terms? That's not enough... Many people in reviews say that it feels like they've come to Europe with authentic French cuisine. 10 years ago, that might have been because there weren't many restaurants like this in Seoul, but now, there are many places with a really nice atmosphere.

Conclusion -
I recommend going somewhere else if possible. There are many other good ones.

I am going to eat the lunch course (gourmet).

The atmosphere was great and the server who looked like Hyun Bin and had a tattoo on his left hand was friendly. We drank sweet wine together and it was very delicious. They told me to eat it separately because it didn't go well with the food, but it actually went well with my taste.
The first amuse bouche was a crispy fried bite-size sandwich topped with caviar. It was crispy and salty.
Onion soup came out second, and it was the most delicious onion soup I've ever had. The harmony of the natural sweetness of the onions and the cheese was good, so it was delicious to dip into the crispy baguette served as an aperitif.
The third dish came with snails, and it tasted like whelk in a creamy risotto-like sauce. I was a little embarrassed to see large tomatoes instead of snails in the bowl space where snails would have been, but it was nice to eat the cream with baguette bread.
The main dish came with lamb shoulder. The main dish was the worst. It was a bit tough, so it didn't break easily, and it didn't go well with the sauce.
Lastly, there was only one dessert to come. It was a thick piece of chocolat, and I felt frustrated because my throat was sore when I ate it. It's difficult to order a drink in the middle of the meal, and they usually give you tea or Americano with dessert, but here they only gave me dessert, so I wondered if I was the only one who didn't get the service.
First of all, they didn't give me wet towels as soon as I sat down at the table, so I was wondering if they weren't there, but when someone else with a reservation came, they were given wet towels. And it was inconvenient to have all the food spilled on the table between meals. The atmosphere was nice and the taste wasn't bad, but some of the service was disappointing. I won't visit again, but I enjoyed the meal.

I was originally going to go to the famous 'Black and White Chef' restaurant, but there were no seats at all, so I decided to go to a Michelin-recommended French restaurant instead. The name 'Sonnet' means sonnet, and the entire menu is composed like a short and cheerful poem. Inside, bar seating is arranged around the open kitchen. Our group of 5 sat in a private room with heating and service, perfect for concentrating on the food.

They only offer a set menu (117,000 won), and although there is no choice, the chef's composition is very good.

In particular, the various finger foods including 'Sweet Shrimp Pie' were excellent. 'Tea' (a type of tartare) with sea urchin roe sauce and perilla leaves provided a rich and rich taste.

The 'Cigar Roll' is chicken liver mousse wrapped in a cocoa-flavored crust and topped with truffle and raspberry sauce, creating a truly sophisticated gastronomic experience with a rich yet subtle blend of sweet and sour.

'Truffle Pancakes' are coated with smoked butter and boast a unique and pleasant aroma.

For the main course, the duck breast (no additional charge) boasts crispy skin and tender flesh, with the rich flavor neutralized by slightly bitter red chicory.

Upgrade to Korean beef (+25,000 won) and experience the culmination of perfect cooking techniques. Perfectly ripe and pink on the outside, juicy on the inside, the flavor spreads throughout your mouth, making each bite a delight.

Attentive service and carefully plated dishes create a comfortable and satisfying dining experience.

reviews.author: My own reasons
reviews.text:
As you walk along Apgujeong Rodeo Street, ‘Wingstop Apgujeong Rodeo Branch’, which has recently emerged as a hot place, catches your eye. This chicken wing restaurant, which originated in the United States, has become very popular among foreigners and young people as soon as it opened.

Even while I was eating it, people around me expressed their admiration, saying, “It’s still so delicious, just like the taste I had in the US!” In this way, Wingstop seems to be especially loved by foreigners who are looking for the taste they have missed abroad by replicating the taste of the original place.

Wing Stop Apgujeong Rodeo branch offers a variety of chicken wings and side menus, and there are also a variety of menus to suit the tastes of Korean customers who prefer spicy flavors. The store's interior creates a modern yet comfortable atmosphere, making it a suitable place for gatherings with friends or for a date.

Combined with the trendy atmosphere of Apgujeong Rodeo, Wingstop is establishing itself as a new attraction in the area. Especially on weekend evenings, you can often see the store crowded, which is probably proof that a lot of people are visiting this place.

Overall, Wingstop Apgujeong Rodeo branch is considered the best place for foreigners who want to enjoy authentic American tastes and the younger generation who seek new tastes and experiences, and the comfortable atmosphere seems to provide visitors with an unforgettable experience.

#Sinsa-dong #Five Guys #Apgujeong

“Korean Five Guys is soft.”

Was it 2 years ago?
The boom we saw when Five Guys launched in Korea was truly incredible.
As time passed, there was no line at the time of launch and even delivery was available, so I ordered delivery because I wanted to taste the Korean Five Guys.
Since I have already experienced it many times in many countries, I know the combination of sauces and toppings that best suits me, so ordering delivery is not difficult.

That's how I felt when I took just one bite of the burger I received.
The characteristic of Five Guys burgers is their very heavy and dense texture and taste, but the Korean texture is definitely softer.
It's not as soft as Shake Shack, but it doesn't have the stiffness of the American mainland.

I enjoyed it more than I expected.
It's not the soft chewy Korean Five Guys burger.

It would be best to order the original size.

reviews.author: ANNEZUE
reviews.text:
I had dinner. The door was locked and the inside was covered with a curtain, so I thought it wasn't open yet because the break time wasn't over, so I stood in front of the entrance shivering in the cold winter weather, waiting for the door to open. Just as I was about to lose my senses to my ears, a man who appeared to be a valet came from the back of the building and told me that I had to ring the bell to enter. I was grateful for the information, but at the same time, it was really annoying. Not only was it difficult to find the bell, there were no horses or staff to guide you, and no separate guidance was given when making a reservation. The inside was dark and narrow. I could see the kitchen, but they were cooking in the darkness like a cave, relying on stand lights.
The first dish was perilla leaf juice. It had a strong perilla leaf scent, but it tasted like sweet vegetable juice. It was a fun taste that I experienced for the first time.
The second dish came out like a mysterious ring tart with mussel meat inside a ring cookie made from red cabbage. It was so delicious that I looked forward to the next dishes. The food hanging on the tree branches was also creative.
The third dish was a dish where when you lift the clam, the smoke trapped in the cheek comes out. The smoke smelled like seaweed, and the chewy scallops and pickled plums went really well together.
The fourth dish was a glutinous rice donut on top, and the unique plating was impressive. The powder sprinkled on top was savory soybean powder, and it was good because it was fried and warm. When I took a bite, it was sticky and sticky, like glutinous rice cake and fried rice cake.
The fifth dish was pumpkin. It was a dish eaten with pumpkin leaves poured over it, and the crunchy pumpkin and fried glutinous rice underneath were unique and delicious.
The sixth dish was a chocolate-coated dried persimmon dish inside a wooden bookshelf, and it was fun for me to open it. On the left page, there was a traditional fairy tale about a tiger and dried persimmons, and the ingredients inside the chocolate dried persimmons were said to be secret, but it tasted like seafood mixed with sweet soybean paste cream.
For the seventh dish, I had to put the napkin on my lap, stand up, put my mask back on, and go to the entrance of the kitchen to get the food myself. It was very uncomfortable. At the entrance to Bueok, I listened to a description of the food while watching yellowtail wrapped in kelp being grilled on charcoal, but it wasn't worth the hassle. I liked the crispy texture of the Cascris Pie, and it tasted like the flounder I tried mixed with mayonnaise. They said it was Korean self-service, but it was funny.
Because the place was small and there were no separate rooms, foreign groups came and talked really loudly. I couldn't get the food explanation properly because the noise was drowned out, and I wanted to eat quietly, but it was uncomfortable. There was a foreign chef and a foreign server in the kitchen, and he had tattoos all over his arms. It was not nice to see him wearing short sleeves while serving and explaining the food.
For the eighth time, sikhye shaved ice using green tea was released. The glutinous rice had a chewy rice cake-like texture. I really liked the three sour-tasting ants on top of the shaved ice. It was truly shocking. I tried to eat it with my eyes closed, but when I saw the ants' bodies, legs, and faces, I couldn't eat them. In the end, I took a napkin and ate some ice sikhye.
The ninth dish was served in a hat-shaped bowl. This was the most delicious. It was a dish of 48-hour braised ribs, abalone intestine sauce, and black crispy perilla seed cookies, so you break the cookies and eat the sauce and meat together. The onion-like sweetness of the sauce and the refreshing taste of the seafood were very delicious.
The tenth dish was buckwheat noodles. It was made from buckwheat noodles and had a chewy texture, but it tasted like ordinary udon noodles. The broth was made with white kimchi and mushroom broth, and the garnish was shiitake mushrooms made with soy sauce, but I had to put the broth and garnish on the noodles myself. The explanation was grand, but the food was boring and disappointing.
The eleventh main dish, the mallard duck, came out. It was my first time seeing mallard ducks. The knife looks really scary. It was like a knife from a raw fish restaurant. It had a peculiar duck smell and was tough. It wasn't exactly good.
The twelfth dish was dessert. He said it contained tangerines, hallabong, yogwa, and cherries. It was like eating heat-killing ice cream, yuzu meringue, and refreshing tangerine shaved ice.
The thirteenth dish included four refreshments and tea. It was pure tea, and it was poured in a ceramic bowl, but there was a strange gunpowder-like smell coming from the cup. The refreshments included a tart topped with acorn jelly, cookies made with pine nuts, marshmallows made with Ssanghwatang, and fudge wrapped in edible paper. The tart was the most delicious and unique food. The noisy restaurant atmosphere and some of the systems were very disappointing, and it was difficult to be satisfied with the meal.
I don't think I'll visit again, but I think it's okay to go for a meal at least once.

Especially since I visited in December, the entire store had a warm atmosphere filled with Christmas designs and various goods, which made me feel good from the moment I entered.

The store was full of character, and the limited-time Christmas props and displays placed throughout the store were so pretty that there were many great photo opportunities. A variety of goods also caught my eye, and there was a wide variety of cups, mugs, stickers, dolls, etc., so it was fun to look at them. If you like character goods, this place alone is worth stopping by.

The coffee was also better than expected. The taste was well-balanced with acidity, so I got the feeling that this place paid attention not only to the design but also to the taste of the coffee. I was able to fully enjoy the holiday atmosphere as I sat in a seat full of Christmas mood while holding a glass of warm drink.

The staff were friendly and the store was well maintained, so my overall stay was comfortable.
If you want to enjoy an emotional atmosphere, seasonal displays, delicious coffee, and various goods all at once in Apgujeong, Iyaiya & Friends is a truly attractive space.

I highly recommend it to anyone who wants to feel the end-of-the-year feeling!

reviews.author: Jiyoung Lee
reviews.text:
Spend a special day at a place where you can enjoy the atmosphere of Apgujeong Rodeo while enjoying a leisurely brunch!
I found this cafe by chance while walking near Dosan Park, and the atmosphere was really special. ‘Iyaiya & Friends’ felt more like a small brand exhibition space rather than a simple cafe, and the interior was decorated with cute characters and emotional interiors, so I felt good the moment I walked in.
The drinks were more delicious than expected, and the signature menu in particular had a pretty look, making it great for taking pictures. I was satisfied with the dessert as it was presented neatly and tastefully.
One of the biggest attractions of this place is that they sell character goods, and it felt like I was in a small pop-up store. I would especially recommend it to those who like goods or stationery, and there were many attractive items that could be used as gifts.
It's close to Apgujeong Rodeo Station, so it's easily accessible, and it's the perfect location to stop by after a walk in Dosan Park. However, it can be crowded on weekends, so if you want to enjoy it leisurely, we recommend visiting on a weekday morning.
It was a cafe that I was satisfied with in terms of sensibility, space, and character, and it is a place I would like to visit again next time. I definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a cafe with a special atmosphere near Apgujeong or Dosan Park!

Above all, the service was the worst. The wooden interior had a warm atmosphere, but there was no bell at the table, no matter how many times I called, no one came, and there were no napkins or wet tissues at the table, so I asked for it, but they forgot, so I had to ask for it again. He didn't show up, so I had to wait. He looked like a model, but he didn't have any sense or intelligence, so it was very frustrating.
After eating, I ordered toast for dessert, but there was no space to put it on the table. If you've already finished your meal and there's no space to put dessert, shouldn't you clear the table first? After asking them to clean it up, we collected the dishes and gave them to them, and only then did they put out the dessert and remove the food dishes, leaving the plate in front of us where we had been eating. The food I ate was all over the place, and the spoon I ate had pasta residue, oil, and food on it, but they didn't seem to have any intention of giving me dessert utensils. When I asked them to clean up the dishes, they just picked up the spoon and fork from the table. They picked it up carelessly, so the pasta oil from the utensil spilled all over the table and floor and got into my drink. I was angry, but I held back for fear of ruining the atmosphere. If you brought your own utensils, you should have given them dessert utensils, but they didn't. So I called the server to ask for dessert utensils, and he came really late. He did everything he was supposed to do and came after taking our order and serving the food. When I came and asked for dessert cutlery, they brought it to me right away. Service training is urgent. It was quite shocking and I will never visit again.
The warm green sauce is unique because it has a sweet yellow sauce and goes well with foods such as vegetables and toast. I enjoyed it.

reviews.text:
#Cheongdam-dong #Oasis

It's my family's favorite restaurant, but I haven't even written a review yet.. haha
Since this is a very famous place, everyone knows that the eggs benedict here is delicious. Let me introduce you to other delicious menu items.

#Reuben Sandwich
It's a very famous sandwich in the U.S., but there's no place in Korea that makes it deliciously, so it was a sad dish. However, Oasis makes it really delicious under the name “The Reuben.”
Oasis bread is really good.
The sturdy whole wheat bread gives the outside and inside taste the real flavor, and it is topped with a quality pastrami that is rarely found in Korea. And the light Munster cheese goes well with it (actually, Swiss cheese should go on top... haha). The only thing that's disappointing is that it would be perfect if served with delicious sauerkraut, but I can't help but appease the disappointment with pickled cucumbers and coleslaw.
Although there aren't many places that sell it, it was by far the best Reuben I've had in Korea so far.

#Beef Baked Bean Chili
There aren't many restaurants that serve this menu, but here at Oasis, they make it really delicious. Most famous brunch restaurants in California have a Mexican-style brunch menu, and this menu also has poached eggs on top, making it very Mexican and satisfying.
Delicious bean chili with a rich umami flavor goes well with soft poached eggs. The thick bacon here is famous, and its salty taste gives you the satisfaction of sweet chili and sweet saltiness. I don't remember the type of bread served with it, but I think it was a delicious brioche-like soft bread. It tastes amazing when you top it with chili.

#Other menus
Basically, the eggs Benedict here is really good because the poached eggs are cooked well. Of course, the hollandaise sauce is also top-notch. The omelette is made in an American style, so it feels rich (actually, the French omelette is a bit cringy haha).

I think the reason the menu here is delicious is because each element is good. The sauce is delicious, the thick cut bacon is generous, and the spinach and grilled tomatoes are also great ingredients.

#Opening time
When I first came to Korea, I found it really absurd that most brunch places didn't open until 11 a.m., but this place opened at 8 a.m. (as I remember). So it became our family's designated brunch place, and although it now opens at 9 a.m., it still opens early in the morning so you can eat comfortably.

However, as it has become more popular, there will be a wait if you go after 9:30, so you have to hurry to eat comfortably.

Also, on weekday mornings, there are many mothers' gatherings, so it is unexpectedly crowded, so please keep that in mind. (Mothers are usually there from around 10 a.m. to 2-3 p.m., so it would be easier to use if you know that.)

This is Baekmidang, an ice cream specialty cafe located in Nonhyeon-dong. This is a premium branch operated by Baekmidang. Even though it is a franchise brand, the interior design is quite outstanding compared to other cafes in Cheongdam-dong.

I usually like Baekmidang's vanilla ice cream, but the frappe style ice cream served with red beans was delicious. The sweet persimmon flavored ice cream wasn't very good. The coffee had a slightly bitter taste as it was eaten with ice cream. It's slightly inferior to other premium coffee brands, but the combination with ice cream is not bad.

The service is ok.

The interior has a nice atmosphere, but it has its drawbacks. The spacing between tables is narrow compared to other cafes in Cheongdam-dong. This is a place where many blind dates and after-parties take place, but it is not suitable for such purposes as it is too bright and the spacing between tables is narrow.

It was a nice cafe with valet parking and a nice atmosphere.

The bathroom was a building bathroom, but it was a private bathroom and was clean, but it was a shared bathroom. And since the lock is a number key, you have to manually lock it from the inside to use it, but you have to lock the one with the number key.

I locked the door below, but someone tried to open the door, so I quickly closed it. So it was a bit inconvenient to use.

I went with a group of 4 and ordered 2 hot Americanos, 2 cold Americanos, and a hot latte, all decaffeinated.

I also ordered one Basque cheesecake, original and chocolate. As expected, most of the original ones are delicious. It's a little disappointing that I couldn't take a picture of the side of the cake.

The center part was soft and delicious, like a cream puff, but I ate all of the original and had some chocolate left over. I recommend trying the original.

1. Due to the large number of people waiting, the usage time is inevitably limited to 2 hours.

2. If possible, please use a table appropriate for the number of people.

reviews.text: On the first floor, place your bread, order coffee, and pay together. Finished bread can be taken directly to the second floor, but brunch or toast must wait for it to be cooked. reviews.text:
There was a wait on the weekend evening, so I went again for lunch on a weekday. There is a bread showcase on the first floor and tables and seats on the 2nd to 4th floors, but drinks must be picked up separately on the 2nd floor.

I like that they have a brunch menu so you can enjoy not just the bread. I ordered salted butter bread, a signature menu item at Standard Bread Dosan branch, and couldn't help but eat it, but it was delicious even when eaten on its own. Since the butter is concentrated at the bottom of the bread, it is much more flavorful when cut or torn lengthwise.

Eggs in Hell is soft and delicious without being overpowering. The meatballs have a kick, and eating them with bread makes them twice as delicious. Mushroom cream pasta is very savory. Try this with bread too. I keep taking it. The ricotta garden salad is decent and the ricotta cheese is delicious.

It's a bakery cafe with a large space and atmosphere, so it's great for chatting and just enjoying drinks. The drink we had together was Tropical Squash, and it was refreshing and green even without carbonation, so it was nice.
I am satisfied overall except for the price of the bread.

reviews.author: Because he’s a genius
reviews.text:
The interior atmosphere has a slightly vintage and emotional feel. It has a different charm from cafes these days.
To conclude, even I, who doesn't like sweet food, enjoyed it satisfactorily, so it's a place worth recommending at least once.
However, it is best not to expect good value for money.

Although the cake looks intense from the outside, it is not overly sweet thanks to the dark chocolate, making it easier to eat (than you might think).
Perhaps because I love chocolate so much, when I take a bite, the deep scent of cacao comes to my mind.
Even though it was a peanut butter cake, it was impressive that the peanut butter wasn't too much, naturally bringing out the cake's natural flavor.
Even among domestic reviewers, there were many comments saying, “This is a place that takes advantage of the quality of its ingredients.”

The coffee is decent. If it costs around 4,000 won, it would be considered excellent, but since it sells for around 6,000 won around here, it provides the basics.
Due to the nature of the neighborhood called Sinsa-dong, you should take the price into consideration, but don't have high expectations.
Overall, I think it's a place worth stopping by if you want to taste desserts made with good ingredients in a unique atmosphere at least once.
